topic: How high-stimulus environments degrade enjoyment of low-stimulus activities
body:
**The things you used to love — reading, long walks, building things — feel flat now. That's not you. That's your threshold.**

When you expose your brain to high-frequency, high-intensity reward signals consistently, it compensates. It downregulates sensitivity to keep things balanced. This is normal. The problem is that downregulation isn't selective. When sensitivity drops, it drops across the board. Everything registers as less rewarding — including the things that used to sustain you.

So you're not a different person. You haven't lost your taste for depth. The signal those activities produce hasn't changed. Your ability to receive it has.

This is reversible. It's not a personality shift. It's a calibration state. And calibration states can be changed.

The restoration process is exactly what it sounds like — removing the high-frequency inputs for long enough that the system recalibrates upward. As sensitivity returns, low-stimulation activities start to register again. The flat feeling lifts.

That person who could read for two hours and feel satisfied at the end of it — they're not gone. The settings are wrong.

Protocol is in the link in bio.
